page: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine within the Cloud Compute family. It features 6 shared vCPUs mapped from 3 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.0 GHz, supporting hyper-threading. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 320 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the weak and poor categories, respectively, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and modest 2.0 GHz clock speed. However, multi-core stress-ng performance reaches average levels, and Redis SET operations demonstrate a solid average throughput of 6.15 million operations per second. Memory read bandwidth is average at 407.68 GB/sec for small cached blocks, though uncached write bandwidth drops to a weak 18.72 GB/sec.

The shared CPU architecture introduces potential resource contention, making this server less suitable for sustained high-compute tasks like single-threaded compression or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation for a 7B model is poor at 4.66 tokens/sec. However, the generous 320 GB NVMe SSD storage and balanced memory capacity offer qualitative cost efficiency for budget-conscious deployments. This server is best suited for multi-threaded web serving, lightweight database operations, development environments, and general-purpose workloads that can tolerate shared CPU performance.
